newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian Deputy PM Nemtsov is a proven reformist.
newsitem.headline: New Russian Deputy PM Nemtsov is a proven reformist.

text.p: Boris Nemtsov, the regional governor who has accepted a post as First Deputy Prime Minister in a new Russian government, is widely respected for putting all his local power behind privatisation, economists said on Monday.
Nemtsov, a boyish 37-year-old, is the governor of Nizhny Novgorod region, 400 kilometers to the east of Moscow and a hotbed of market reforms.

"There is absolutely no question that he deserves his reputation as a reformer," said Chris Williams, a project manager at the International Finance Corp (IFC), the World Bank affiliate, which has a high-profile project in the region.
"He has been a real source of support as well as great ideas. I've seen him working with high-level foreign officials and state farms and he is effective at every level."
Nemtsov and the IFC's flagship farm privatisation programme in the region has had critics in Russia but the former can point to success stories in turning around failing Soviet-era collectives.
IFC figures show that of about 250 reformed agricultural units in Russia, 166 of those are in Nizhny Novgorod region.
President Boris Yeltsin offered Nemtsov the first deputy premiership alongside Anatoly Chubais, who led early Russian privatisation efforts. Nemtsov accepted, the Kremlin said.
"Two young men -- you and Anatoly Chubais -- create a fresh young team in the government -- from scratch," Yeltsin told Nemtsov on television on Monday.
"No one (else) has been appointed yet. All candidates to the government would be agreed with the two first deputy premiers."
Nizhny Novgorod region, whose eponymous car-making capital was a closed city in the Soviet era under the name Gorky, also has small business privatisation and other reform programmes.
Nemtsov, considered to be a practical business-minded administrator, is seen as potential Presidential material.

"Reportedly he is not easy to deal with because his own interests are maximising the value of his holdings -- the city or the region. He does not sell out the area, which could be good when parlayed to a federal level," said James Fenkner, director of research at CentreInvest Securities.
Poul Funder Larsen, senior analyst at Rye, Man and Gor Securities, said that a visit to the Nizhny region showed tangible benefits of reform.

"You get the feeling that people have felt at least some kind of small concrete pluses of reform going on," he said. "The small business sector is very strong down there and it actually seems to be working."

Nemtsov, who was sent as a presidential representative to Nizhny by President Boris Yeltsin shortly after the breakup of the Soviet Union, has invited foreign organisations such as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the IFC to the area.

Funder Larsen gave Nemtsov credit for helping automaker AO Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod (GAZ) GAZA.RTS, producer of the ubiquitous Volga sedan, to open up to foreign involvement and attract foreign aid.

"The industry in Nizhny oblast (region) is doing fairly well, and I think he has played a significant role, such as with GAZ. It is the only one of the main Russian plants that has been able to increase its market share," said Funder Larsen.
"The changes are not so much on the legal level, but like a lot of places in Russia, when the regional government puts its authority behind such programmes, it trickles down to lower levels."
